judgments.reasoning_cat1: A statutory disclosure notice that recites the TRIA definition of terrorism verbatim; it is descriptive rather than operative, and its terms are fixed by federal certification rather than by construction.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It says the policy 'makes available' terrorism insurance, which sits somewhat oddly with the $-0- terrorism premium in c005 and the war/insurrection exclusion at c093, but a notice form is unlikely to be pitted against the operative Crime exclusions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A plain recital of the federal reimbursement formula with a single fixed percentage; nothing in the wording admits two readings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing in the Crime Coverage Section or General Terms addresses federal reimbursement, so there is no provision for it to collide with.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A numeric cap statement; the only blemish is the OCR run-together 'ina Program Year', which does not change meaning.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It duplicates c004 in substance but the two are consistent (Treasury cap vs insurer cap), so no genuine internal inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite terms — an aggregate threshold, a deductible condition and pro rata allocation by Treasury procedures; no term needs construing.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It restates c003 from the insurer's side and does not touch the Crime limits of liability in c116, so the fit is clean.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single blank-filled figure of $-0-; it states a fact rather than a right and carries no ambiguous term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A zero terrorism premium is in mild tension with c001's statement that the policy 'makes available' terrorism insurance, but the premium bill and the notice are both non-operative.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An informational statement about producer compensation with a website and phone number; it creates no obligation to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No other provision of the policy addresses producer compensation, so there is nothing to reconcile it against.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A notice identifying which coverage sections are claims-made; the sentence is clear on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It describes Executive Liability, EPL and Fiduciary coverage sections that Item 3 of the Declarations does not list as purchased (only General Terms, Crime and Special Coverage), a mismatch between the notice and the Coverage Summary.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conditional statement about retroactive dates; 'if a claims-made coverage section contains' is expressly contingent and unambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No coverage section in this policy contains a retroactive date and none of the named claims-made sections was purchased, so the clause is orphaned but not contradicted.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard claims-made explanatory language; 'claims actually made or incidents reported' is a familiar formulation with no live ambiguity here.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Crime Coverage Section is a discovery-based, not claims-made, cover, so this notice pulls against Crime Exclusion 19 (c110/c134) and Subsection 25 (c116/c130) if read as applying to it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Detailed and specific about the 60-day automatic and one-year optional extended reporting periods; the terms are numerically fixed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It grants extended reporting rights only for coverage sections not purchased under this policy, and the Crime section instead uses a 60-day post-termination discovery window in c110 — parallel but different mechanisms.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A commercial explanation of claims-made rate maturity; it confers no rights and uses no operative term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing else in the instrument addresses premium maturity, so there is no provision to check it against.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An all-caps Declarations warning; the quoted terms are all defined elsewhere and the sentence structure is standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It warns that limits will be eroded by 'DEFENSE COSTS' and that retentions apply, but the Crime section has no Defense Costs concept and c057 expressly says no retention applies to Investigative Expenses — a mismatch with the purchased coverage.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A boilerplate consideration recital subject to the rest of the policy; nothing in it is capable of two readings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It defers to the Declarations and all other terms, and c015 supplies the priority rule, so it cannot itself conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Six words — 'Coverage shall extend anywhere in the world' — absolute on its face, but very short absolutes of this kind are exactly what parties fight about at the margins.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is expressly cut back by the trade sanctions endorsement c045 and is in tension with definitions keyed to US chartering (c069 Executive) and US/Canadian currency (c078), though c015 gives coverage-section terms priority.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The words 'inconsistent or in conflict' are the operative trigger and are not self-defining, but the priority rule itself is stated plainly.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: This is the instrument's own conflict-resolution rule, so it is the provision a court would reach for when reconciling the General Terms notice clause c021 with Crime Subsection 27 (c118) or the endorsements — a role that makes it a candidate for construction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A pure cross-reference definition; the term simply takes the meaning given in the applicable coverage section.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Crime Coverage Section contains no definition of 'Claim' at all, yet c021 and Endorsement 1 (c039-c043) impose Claim-notice machinery — leaving 'Claim' undefined for the only purchased liability cover.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line referral definition with no ambiguous term of its own.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Crime Subsection 11 does define Insured (c074), so the referral resolves cleanly for this coverage section.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Identifies the Parent Organization by pointing to a specific Declarations item; entirely determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Item 1 names MEDIDATA SOLUTIONS INC. consistently in both Declarations, while Item 4 of the Crime Declarations spells it 'Medidate Solutions, Inc.', a discrepancy that touches c080 more than this clause.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Defines the period by reference to Item 2 and adds a proportionality rule for short or long periods; both limbs are specific.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Item 2 as printed reads 'To 42:01 A.M.' — an obvious typographic corruption of 12:01 — and Endorsement 3 (c130) changes what must occur 'during the Policy Period' from sustaining loss to discovering it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: States separateness of limits and retentions in plain terms, twice qualified by 'unless stated to the contrary'; nothing needs construing.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is consistent with Crime Subsection 25 (c116) and the per-Insuring-Clause limits in the Crime Declarations.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Long but concrete — designated addresses, effective dates on receipt, and an excuse for late notice where 'not reasonably possible', a standard and workable formula.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its general late-notice safe harbour sits alongside the different regime in Endorsement 1 (c039-c041, prejudice-based) and the strict condition precedent with 90-day and six-month deadlines in Crime Subsection 27 (c118), which c015 says would control.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Names a specific publication and three specific trigger dates for conversion; the mechanics are determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Crime Subsection 28 (c119) sets its own foreign currency rule keyed to the date of Discovery, which differs from this clause's judgment/settlement/loss-due triggers, though the opening 'Except as otherwise provided' harmonises them.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional subrogation and cooperation clause; 'everything necessary' is broad but is a familiar and workable standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It reads consistently with the Recoveries waterfall in c120, which allocates recoveries after payment rather than contradicting subrogation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Full compliance with all the terms of this policy' as a condition precedent is a sweeping, one-sided formulation whose reach against a minor breach is genuinely contestable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is hard to square with c021's and Endorsement 1's express rules that a late notice does not invalidate coverage absent prejudice, and with the two-year suit limitation in c118.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An enumerated agency list with one express carve-out; the enumeration is closed and specific.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The exception for 'giving of notice to apply for an Extended Reporting Period' refers to a mechanism the purchased Crime section does not contain, a small orphan reference.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An exclusive-formalities clause naming the required signatory; definite and easily applied.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The endorsements are signed only by an 'Authorized Representative' with an illegible mark, which is at least arguably short of 'an authorized employee of Chubb & Son' — but no party disputed endorsement validity.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A specific 20-day notice rule for the first 60 days, driven by New York statute; the numbers leave nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It fits the structure of the rest of Subsection 11 and the notice-copy requirement in c034.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An enumerated list of statutory termination grounds; item (iv) turns on 'substantially and materially increases the hazard', a genuinely elastic standard, and (v) on 'material change in the nature or extent of the risk'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The grounds are exhaustive and consistent with c027 and c035's requirement that the notice state the specific reason.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short and mechanical rule for insured-initiated termination keyed to written notice before the effective date.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It dovetails with the short-rate refund rule in c032, which expressly addresses termination by the Parent Organization.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'At such other time as may be agreed upon' is open-ended by design; mutual agreement supplies the content.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is the residual limb of an otherwise closed list and does not undercut any other termination mechanism.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Expiration and nonrenewal keyed to Item 2 with an express cross-reference to paragraph (g); definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The cross-reference to paragraph (g) is accurate and paragraph (g) (c033) delivers the promised notice machinery.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Customary short rates' is an undefined trade term whose computation is not spelled out anywhere in the policy.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is consistent with the termination grid in c027-c031 and nothing else in the instrument sets a refund basis.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Long but almost entirely numeric — 60/120 days, 10% of expiring rate, 30-day and 60-day sub-rules — and each contingency is separately addressed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sub-paragraph (iii) increases aggregate limits pro rata for extensions, which interacts with but does not contradict the Policy Period proportionality rule in c019.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single mechanical obligation to copy the broker at its last known address; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is consistent with the notice obligations elsewhere in Subsection 11.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Requires the notice to state specific reasons and an effective date; short and determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: In the source text this sub-paragraph runs directly into the heading of Subsection 12, an OCR/formatting merger, but the substantive fit with c027-c033 is clean.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Terminates prior bonds identified in Item 4 as of inception; the reference is specific and self-executing.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps with the last paragraph of Crime Subsection 24 (c115), which Endorsement 3 (c129) deletes in its entirety — leaving this General Terms provision as the only surviving prior-bond termination rule.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-sentence bankruptcy clause preserving the insurer's rights and obligations; standard and clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing elsewhere addresses insured insolvency, so there is no counterpart to conflict with.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A headings-are-not-substantive clause; about as determinate as drafting gets.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is repeated in each endorsement (c044, c046, c123, c126, c131, c133, c135) consistently, so no incoherence arises.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Has prejudiced the Company' is the operative trigger and is an inherently fact-laden standard, but it is the statutory New York formula and is qualified expressly by paragraph (2).
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It relaxes the notice consequences that c021 and the condition-precedent language of Crime Subsection 27 (c118) impose, and c024 still says no action lies without 'full compliance with all the terms' — a real pull in opposite directions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Not reasonably possible' and 'as soon as reasonably possible' are elastic, but they are settled statutory phrases and mirror the same words in c021.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It duplicates the last paragraph of c021 almost word for word, so the two are consistent rather than in conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clean two-year burden-shifting rule with an irrebuttable presumption; the categories are specific and the numbers fixed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The endorsement's paragraph numbering is scrambled in the text (the '(1) (2) (3) (4)' block appears together in c039), so which paragraph 'the above paragraph' refers to is not obvious on the face of the assembled document.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A narrow saving clause preserving claims-made timing and barring duplicate coverage; specific in what it preserves.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It preserves 'claims made during the Policy Period' rules that exist only in unpurchased coverage sections, so it has little to operate on in a Crime-only policy.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Death or personal injury, as that term is defined by the New York Insurance Law' anchors the key phrase to an external statute, but the direct-action right and 60-day carve-out are otherwise mechanical.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It says the injured person may sue 'notwithstanding any other provision', which flatly cuts across c024's bar on joining or impleading the Company in any action.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Boilerplate headings and 'all other terms remain unchanged'; nothing susceptible of two readings in isolation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 'All other terms shall remain unchanged' is the phrase that has to absorb the competing amendments to Exclusion 19 in c127 and c134, but that strain shows up in those clauses, not here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'To the extent that trade or economic sanctions or other similar laws or regulations prohibit' is a general catch-all with no enumerated specifics to anchor it, and its reach is genuinely open.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cuts back the unqualified worldwide grant in c014 without saying so, and c015's priority rule does not obviously resolve which prevails.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Identical headings boilerplate to c044; determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the corresponding clauses in every other endorsement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A consideration recital subordinating the coverage section to the Declarations and General Terms; no operative ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It says the coverage section is subject to the General Terms while c015 says coverage-section terms control over inconsistent General Terms — a circularity, though the standard reading harmonises them.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Direct loss' is the load-bearing and undefined phrase, and 'in collusion with others' broadens the grant, but the clause is short and its elements are all defined terms.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It says loss 'sustained by an Insured' whereas the parallel clauses 2-8 say 'sustained by an Organization', and Ownership (c111) and Exclusion 13 (c104) both cut it back; c112 also rewrites it wholesale for ERISA Plans.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An itemised premises grant with four enumerated sub-limbs; the closing 'committed by a Third Party' qualifier is oddly placed and its reach over sub-limbs (i)-(iv) is not obvious.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exclusions 14 (c105) and 15 (c106) carve it back in specific and consistent ways, and it did not bear on the wire-transfer loss at issue.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Same structure as the premises clause with the same trailing 'committed by a Third Party' qualifier, plus 'temporarily within the home of an Employee or an Organization', which is odd applied to an entity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It reads consistently with the In Transit definition (c075) and Exclusion 14 (c105), which excepts carriers for hire other than armored car companies.
